newsitem.title: zaire: Zaire rebel commander killed - security sources.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel commander killed - security sources.

text.p: The military commander of rebels in eastern Zaire was killed in an ambush earlier this month, security sources in the region said on Monday.
They said said Andre Kisase Ngandu was killed on or about January 8 near the rebel-held town of Butembo. For several days residents in Goma, the rebel capital, have reported rumours of his death.
The sources in the region, speaking to Reuters in Nairobi by telephone, declined to be identified or quoted by name.
Laurent Kabila, chairman of the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), has yet to announce his chief lieutenant's death.
"His death has been a big blow for the rebels but they are getting by," one security source said.
The Alliance rebels hold a swath of eastern Zaire, bordering Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi, after a lightning offensive that began last October against Zaire's ragged army.
Zaire is threatening to launch a major counter-offensive to recover the lost territory.
Like Kabila, Ngandu was a veteran foe of Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko who seized power in 1965. Mobutu is ailing with cancer and returned for treatment in Europe this month.
Ngandu was chairman of the National Resistance Council for Democracy (CNRD), one of the Alliance's key components.
A statement faxed to Nairobi on Monday and purporting to come from the CNRD said Major-General Ngandu was assassinated by "armed elements in the service of Kabila".
The statement, dated Goma on Monday but apparently sent from neighbouring Uganda, was signed anonymously by "J.B. of General Ngandu's protocol service".

But the security sources said Ngandu's convoy was ambushed by "Mai-Mai", guerrillas from indigenous tribes in eastern Zaire who at first teamed up with the Alliance forces but later fell out with them.
